title: I Swear I Won’t Bother You Again!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Duke's daughter Violette is jailed after a jealous attempt on her half-sister Maryjune, whom their father favors after returning with his mistress as his new wife. Repenting in prison, Violette finds time rewound to the day she met her sister and resolves to avoid her family and Prince Claudia and become a nun, but she draws attention anyway (Seven Seas blurb via AniList/MU; ANN Manga Guide).
life_message: Repentance and a changed heart can rewrite a life that envy and neglect once ruined.

content.note: Attempted murder of her half-sister in the first timeline (ANN); 'crime of passion' (MU blurb).
Prison and a looming repeat of disaster (blurb, ANN).
Prince and suitors take notice (ANN; MU Reverse Harem); father's affair and child born of infidelity (ANN, MU Adultery).
Opens with Violette starving herself in prison (ANN); parental emotional abuse and neglect (MU Emotional Abuse, Abusive Parent/s; ANN says the manga waters it down).
Jealousy leading to violence is shown as wrong and repented.

dominant: Repentance and second chance; family dysfunction; aristocratic romance

frames.aligns: Contrition in prison, amended life, wish to enter a convent.
frames.concerns: Father's adultery; self-starvation; abuse at home.

frames.aligns: Repentance and turning from envy; monastic longing.
Second-chance grace and forgiveness of a sister.
Withdrawal from worldly ambition; peace with sister.
Sympathy for an abused, neglected child.
frames.concerns: Blame placed on the victim of neglect.

frames.aligns: Karma and a second life to do right.
Envy as source of suffering; renunciation.

frames.concerns: Self-starvation framing; reviewer says abuse is watered down.

frames.aligns: Reform of character; unity in family.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Violette renounces her earlier jealous revenge (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Seeks her own path away from family to a convent (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family ties and favoritism drive the plot (MU).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Wants to 'live out her days peacefully' (ANN).

folkways.japan: A Japanese villainess-reincarnation drama in a European-styled court; the heroine's self-effacing withdrawal reflects Japanese ideals of restraint.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls the manga a fairly standard reborn-villainess story; no preaching noted (to verify).
delivery.note: Parents are shown as negligent; Maryjune is the father's favorite rather than a villain (ANN).

winners_losers: Violette's repentance earns sympathy; the father's favoritism and infidelity are cast as harmful.
to_verify: Self-starvation opening and emotional abuse: ANN says the manga softens the novel's abuse; check how it is shown.
ANN covers volume 1 and recommends the light novel.
